target_customer: Consumers and developers buying wearable hardware: first the Myo gesture armband, then Focals smart glasses sold to consumers
problem: People wanted to control computers and devices without cameras or keyboards, and later to see glanceable notifications without pulling out a phone.
business_model: Consumer hardware sales (Myo armband at 149 dollars at pre-order, Focals originally 1000 dollars)
product_category: Wearable computing hardware (gesture armband, then smart glasses)

founders.name: Stephen Lake
founders.background_notes: Later founded Jetson per YC page.

competitors.name: Leap Motion
competitors.traction_then: Controller to launch spring 2013 at 70 dollars

competitors.name: Microsoft Kinect
competitors.what: Camera based gesture and body tracking

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading muscle electrical signals reliably through a wearable, plus custom hardware, and later holographic laser display glasses, required hardware engineering and signal processing well beyond a small software team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware and signal processing know how were hard to copy, but demand for the Myo faded and big platforms could pursue glasses.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google acquired North in June 2020 for a reported 180 million dollars after weak Focals sales.

market_need_then: Pre-orders were strong: 10,000 in two days and over 30,000 by June 2013 per press, showing consumer and developer curiosity for gesture control.

branding.name_origin: Thalmic Labs was chosen in a rush in 2011 partly because the .com was available (co-founder Aaron Grant). North was chosen in 2018 to suggest Canada and the North Star.
branding.domain_note: Thalmic Labs .com was available at the time of naming; later site at bynorth.com, a prefix style domain.

identity.logo: Rebranded logo with the North name in 2018; designer not found
identity.visual_style: Fashion and lifestyle oriented consumer hardware

rebrands.why: Thalmic Labs sounded too techy for a consumer fashion product

branding.community_and_virality: Press and developer interest around Myo at launch; no merch or fan accounts confirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: Myo got strong early press and pre-orders, and the rename to North was a deliberate consumer move, but the Focals brand did not reach mass sales.

pivots.to: Focals consumer smart glasses under the North name
pivots.why: Seek a larger consumer wearable market; Myo sales were limited

outcome_analysis: Thalmic Labs won early attention with the Myo armband and raised 120 million dollars in 2016, then pivoted to Focals smart glasses at 1000 dollars under the North name. Sales were reportedly weak even after a 400 dollar price cut and cash was short, so Google bought the team for about 180 million dollars in June 2020 and the product line was wound down with refunds.
notes: Company website www.bynorth.com could not be fetched (DNS failure, likely dead or blocked); the YC page was used instead. The acquisition price of 180 million is a Globe and Mail report relayed by others and Google did not disclose it. Total raised reported as over 140 million or 135 million. Sales being weak is reported, not from the company. Series A investor list partly from a search summary. No valuation found for either round.
